newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU oilseeds groups discuss Blair House with ASA.
newsitem.headline: EU oilseeds groups discuss Blair House with ASA.

text.p: German and French oilseeds producer lobbies have scheduled talks with American Soybean Association representatives in Europe to resolve differing views on the EU oilseeds area, a statement from German lobby Ufop said.
The statement said Ufop, French partner organisation FOP and ASA delegates recently held joint talks in Vienna and planned to continue their dialogue. But it gave no timetable or meeting place.
While the groups agreed to promote marketing of seeds derived from genetically modified organisms (GMOs) and industrial uses for oils, they clashed on the area issue.
The bilateral Blair House accord, agreed in 1992 to help finalise the last world trade round under GATT, limits EU oilseeds to 4.934 million hectares plus a compulsory set-aside.
Ufop and FOP wish to renegotiate this limit in the next WTO (World Trade Organisation) round in order to mobilise idle area resources to meet expanding demand.

ASA said the United States would not renegotiate the ceiling agreed in 1992 before the next global trade round because U.S. oilseeds producers had also made sacrifices to comply with market liberalisation under Farm Bill stipulations.
Ufop said world oilseeds output and demand were projected to rise by two percent per annum and the EU was excluded from any participation in such growth.

It demanded the theoretically static Blair House limit should be raised along with demand growth and its inbuilt limit on industrial output corresponding with one million tonnes of soymeal equivalent should be doubled or lifted altogether.
It argued the limit was blocking innovative developments and higher production of environmentally sound raw materials such as bio fuels, lubricants and detergents from rapeseed or sunflowerseed.
ASA also rejected this demand ahead of the next multilateral trading round at the end of the century. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
